design_rationale: The authors explicitly describe the study as a prospective randomized comparison in which 336 patients (receiving 365 catheters) were randomized to either a valved or clamped PICC.

domain_judgments.rationale: The study states patients were randomized, but the specific method of sequence generation and allocation concealment is not reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: After signing the institutional review board-approved informed consent, 336 patients were randomized to receive 365 valved (n = 182) or clamped (n = 183) catheters (Figs. 1 and 2, respectively).

domain_judgments.rationale: Although blinding of staff and participants was not possible due to catheter appearance and flush protocols, care was standardized and analyzed essentially as allocated without problematic post-randomization deviations.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A deficiency of this study was the inability to blind the participants to the type of catheter used, which was not feasible because of the different physical appearances of the catheters and the different flushes administered.

domain_judgments.rationale: Missing outcome data was very low (only 3 patients excluded out of 365 randomized catheters, <1%) and balanced across groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Five patients were lost to follow-up: two after 90 days (considered discontinued at the date of last follow-up), and one each at 1, 3, and 15 days after placement (these patients were excluded from the study).

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were defined by objective clinical and laboratory criteria (such as inability to infuse, positive cultures, and clinical resolution), making outcome assessment unlikely to be significantly biased by lack of blinding.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Follow-up by the PICC nurse occurred on a weekly basis as long as the line was in place. She was notified and made the initial visit in the event of any in-hospital complications such as occlusion, fracture of catheter, local inflammation, or infection.

domain_judgments.rationale: No pre-registered trial protocol is cited or available to evaluate whether outcomes and analyses were selected from multiple eligible options.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Data were collected in a computer database and card file maintained by the PICC nurse. Baseline characteristics of the two groups and differences between treatment groups in measures or events after randomization were compared using the chi-square statistic for discrete variables and the Student's t test for continuous variables.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns due to lack of detailed reporting on sequence generation and allocation concealment in the randomization process, as well as the absence of a pre-registered protocol.

paper_title: 92888204_Journal of Hospital Medicine - 2018 - Kleidon - How Does Your PICCOMPARE  A Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial Comparing
design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated 1:1 to standard care or BioFlo PICC using a computer-generated, web-based central randomization service.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated, concealed via a web-based system, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was computer generated, and web based via Griffith University (https://www151.griffith.edu.au/random) to ensure allocation concealment until study entry. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio with computer-generated and randomly varied block sizes of 2 and 4.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although blinding was not possible due to the nature of the devices, care was standardized according to clinical guidelines with no evidence of non-protocol deviations, and failure to insert in 4 participants was balanced and handled appropriately.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study could not be blinded because study products had to be visible to the clinical and research staff. However, it is unlikely that staff would intentionally sabotage PICCs to bias the study.

domain_judgments.rationale: Follow-up was complete for all 146 participants who had PICC inserted (and 0% attrition across the trial).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: No participants were lost to follow-up, and no primary outcome data were missing.

domain_judgments.rationale: Objective clinical definitions were used for PICC failure and complications, and key diagnostic components (thrombosis, BSI) were evaluated by blinded specialists.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A blinded radiologist and infectious disease specialist reviewed and diagnosed thrombosis of deep veins and catheter-associated BSI outcomes, respectively.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered and followed a published protocol, reporting all prespecified primary and secondary outcomes without evidence of selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was prospectively registered with the Australian Clinical Trials Registry (ACTRN12615001290583), and the research protocol was published.17

overall_summary: The study followed a well-conducted randomized controlled pilot protocol with centralized allocation concealment, complete follow-up, blinded assessment of key objective outcomes, and preregistration, resulting in low risk of bias across all domains.

design_rationale: Participants were explicitly described as being randomized to one of three types of dual lumen PICCs.

domain_judgments.rationale: The authors state that participants were randomized, but they do not report the method of sequence generation or allocation concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Participants were randomized into one of three dual lumen 5 Fr PICCs

domain_judgments.rationale: Although healthcare personnel could not be blinded to catheter type, care followed standardized hospital protocols and only one post-randomization exclusion occurred, with analysis conducted according to randomized groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In one patient, the PICC (Navilyst PASV) could only be advanced a short distance and it was not possible to aspirate blood from it. This patient was excluded from further analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Data were available for 101 of 102 randomized patients (nearly complete follow-up), and the single exclusion was due to technical failure of insertion.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 102 patients were recruited to the study... In one patient, the PICC (Navilyst PASV) could only be advanced a short distance and it was not possible to aspirate blood from it. This patient was excluded from further analysis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Catheter occlusion is an objective mechanical/functional clinical event defined and managed through a standardized clinical protocol, making measurement bias unlikely despite lack of blinding.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: PICC occlusions were recorded and dealt with according to the following protocol. Both withdrawal occlusions and total occlusions were dealt with in the same way and we did not distinguish between the two or document which sort had occurred; 10000u urokinase was diluted into 1 ml 0.9% NaCl in a 10 mL syringe and instilled into each lumen using a push-pull technique.

domain_judgments.rationale: No pre-registered trial protocol or statistical analysis plan is cited, raising some concerns regarding potential selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Power calculations and data analysis was performed in conjunction with the Center for Applied Medical Statistics, University of Cambridge... Analysis was on an intention-to-treat basis (i.e. the data was analyzed according to the groups as randomized).

overall_summary: The study has some concerns overall due to a lack of details regarding the randomization and allocation concealment procedures, as well as the absence of an identifiable pre-registered protocol.

design_rationale: The study is explicitly described as a prospective, randomized controlled trial in which 180 adult oncology patients were randomized into three groups receiving different PICC types.

domain_judgments.rationale: The article states that patients were randomized into three groups, but it does not report the method of sequence generation or allocation concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: One hundred and eighty adult patients candidate to chemotherapy were randomized into three groups: power-injectable PICCs with Solo-2 proximal valve (Bard); power-injectable PICCs with PASV (Pressure Activated Safety Valve) proximal valve (Navilyst); and non-valved power-injectable PICCs (Medcomp).

domain_judgments.rationale: Although blinding of healthcare providers was not possible due to device differences, insertion and catheter care protocols were strictly standardized across groups, and all randomized patients were analyzed according to assigned groups without trial-deviating non-protocol interventions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All PICCs were single lumen 4Fr, inserted according to a well-defined protocol... and managed according to the recommendations of the most recent guidelines... Each PICC was exclusively used while the patient was in the Day Hospital of the Oncology Unit, by the same group of oncology nurses, strictly adopting the policies of our Hospital...

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data appear to be completely accounted for across all 180 enrolled and randomized patients until study termination.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We analyzed the results from the first 180 randomized patients, which yielded quite consistent results. Table I shows the characteristics of the three groups of patients.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome assessors (nurses administering infusions) were aware of the assigned device type, and key endpoints such as difficulties with gravity infusion and partial occlusions relied on subjective nurse assessment via questionnaires.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The main endpoint of the study was to evaluate the incidence of occlusion and malfunction of the catheters. As the definition of these terms is sometimes ambivalent, we prepared a questionnaire for each use of each catheter, which had to be filled by the nurse caring for the PICC on that specific day.

domain_judgments.rationale: There is no mention of a pre-registered trial protocol or pre-specified statistical analysis plan, raising some concerns for selective outcome reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The study was interrupted at 180 patients (approximately 60 for each group) because of three episodes of rupture of Power Solo PICCs... The statistical analysis of the data was performed by standard descriptive statistics; percentages were compared by Chi-square test.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns because the methods for sequence generation and allocation concealment were not described, outcome assessors were unblinded for subjective flow/malfunction evaluations, and no pre-registered protocol was available.

design_rationale: The study is a pilot parallel randomized controlled trial where adult participants were randomly allocated (1:1) to either an intervention or control PICC using a central web-based computer-generated randomization service.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation sequence was computer-generated and concealed using a central web-based service, and baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients who agreed to participate were randomised via computer-generated randomisation immediately before PICC insertion via a web-based service (https://randomisation.griffith.edu.au/) to ensure allocation concealment until study entry. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio with randomly varied block sizes of two and four.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although clinical staff and patients were unblinded, care protocols were standardized across groups, protocol deviations were minimal, and an appropriate intention-to-treat approach was followed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: It was not possible to blind the PICC inserters, patients, or healthcare professionals caring for the patients enrolled in the study... all randomly assigned patients were analysed on an intention-to-treat basis.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary outcome and failure data were completely accounted for, with no withdrawals and balanced right-censoring across study arms due to hospital transfer.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: No patients withdrew from the study; therefore, the retention and attrition criteria of < 15% were met. Thirteen (12%) patients were censored on transfer to another hospital (seven in the standard care and six in the intervention group). There was no missing data for the primary outcome.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome measures for catheter failure and complications followed standardized, objective definitions, and key component outcomes (infections, thrombosis) were blindly adjudicated.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The outcome of device failure was an objective measure, assigned by clinical staff (not research staff or investigators)... The infection control physician (adjudicating infection outcomes), radiologist (adjudicating thrombosis outcomes), and data analyst were blinded to the study allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered and had a published a priori protocol, and all pre-specified feasibility and clinical outcomes are reported according to plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Trial registration: Australia and New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry ACTRN12616001578493. Prospectively registered on 16 November 2016. The trial protocol was published a priori (Kleidon et al., Vasc Access 3:15–21, 2017).

overall_summary: The study was judged to be at low risk of bias across all five RoB 2 domains, with robust central web-based randomization, prospective registration, blinded adjudication for key outcomes, and complete follow-up data.
